label: HackerOne
terms_note: HackerOne Hacker API v1 (HTTP Basic with an API token identifier and value). Rate limits: 600 reads per minute; programs are the bounty programs you can see.

fields.name: api_username
fields.help: API token identifier from https://hackerone.com/settings/api_token/edit (used as the Basic auth username).

fields.name: api_token
fields.help: API token value generated on the same page (used as the Basic auth password).

adapter.rate_note: Docs: 'Read operations: 600 requests per minute'. Five requests per second.

me.note: There is no profile endpoint in the Hacker API; GET /hackers/payments/balance verifies the credentials and returns {data: {balance}}.

discover.note: GET /hackers/programs (page[number], page[size] ≤ 100): the programs visible to you. `id` is the program handle that get_competition takes. No text or status filter, so `query`, `kind` and `status` are not sent; no total in the response. offers_bounties, currency, state and your report counts stay in `raw`.

get_competition.note: GET /hackers/programs/{handle}. `description` is the program policy (markdown). Scope lives at /hackers/programs/{handle}/structured_scopes (not mapped).

my_entries.note: GET /hackers/me/reports: your reports across programs (no program filter, so `competition_id` is not sent). Title, weakness and bounty timestamps stay in `raw`.

not_offered.standings: No leaderboard endpoint in the Hacker API (hacktivity is a disclosed-report feed, not a ranking).
not_offered.enter: No join endpoint: public programs accept reports directly and private programs are invitation-only.
not_offered.submit: POST /hackers/reports requires 'team_handle', 'title', 'vulnerability_information' and 'impact' (all required); the submit vocabulary has no title/impact fields, so it is not mapped.

evidence: host api.hackerone.com: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (DigiCert Inc)
probe: 4/4 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 4/4 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
